findings.summary: The tree-count check can never fire; only a manifest count mismatch can be reached.
findings.evidence: Missing and Extra are checked before the counts, and a git tree cannot hold duplicate paths. So when the tree's paths match C0's, the tree count must match too. Only the manifest count can differ, and only when the manifest repeats an entry. The plan mentions a 'duplicated manifest entry' in decision 3, but the count-mismatch test does not say which tampering it uses. Fix: Say that the count-mismatch test duplicates a manifest entry and asserts CountMismatch with what = manifest. Drop the tree-count check or mark it as a defensive check that cannot be reached.

findings.summary: No error is named for a manifest entry with no C0 file, or a C0 file with no manifest entry.
findings.evidence: The HashMismatch step looks up 'the manifest entry' but does not say what happens when there isn't one. It also does not say what happens when a manifest entry names a path that is not in C0. Fix: Name the variant for each case and test at least one of them using the hook.

findings.summary: The changed-file test does not say which error variant it asserts.
findings.evidence: When bytes change, BlobMismatch fires first in the stated order, so HashMismatch is never reached in this test. The demonstration lists 'BlobMismatch/HashMismatch'. Fix: Have the changed-file test assert BlobMismatch exactly. Keep the separate manifest-hash test asserting HashMismatch.

findings.summary: athena-git lib.rs has no stale text, so this listed deliverable will likely stay unchanged.
findings.evidence: lib.rs:11 reads 'the append-only writer of the athena/records branch'. It has no 'nothing calls' text. Fix: Say that lib.rs is left unchanged, or add a short pointer to the importer there, so the verifier does not expect an edit.

summary: I read the code the plan depends on, and it exists as the plan describes. RecordsWriter::{new, tip, append} and Change::put are in athena-git/src/records_branch.rs. Git::{ls_tree (recursive), show_file, cat_blob, isolated} are in athena-git/src/lib.rs. athena_data::sha256_hex is there. HistoryRecord::parse and ImportManifest::validate are in history.rs, and validate rejects an empty paths list. crate::now() is in athena-core/src/lib.rs. athena-core does not depend on thiserror yet, so adding it is a real change. The stale text the plan wants to fix is real: records_branch.rs:22 ("Nothing calls this writer yet") and records-history.md:276. Checking for an existing tip before writing is the right way to refuse a second import. The writer's own first write expects the all-zero id, so a concurrent first write by someone else is also rejected. Using a private hook to commit deliberately broken imports exercises the self-check on commits that really exist. Each failure demonstration is paired with a passing control, so the tests would fail if the behavior were missing. My findings are all minor or nit. None blocks the plan.
